gaps.sentence: The thunderstorm was absolutely ___ , so the children hid under the blankets (TERRIFY).
gaps.hint: the storm causes the fear (-ing); note 'terrific' means excellent
gaps.explanation: The storm causes terror, so it is terrifying; the children felt terrified. 'Terrific' means excellent.

gaps.sentence: He made a ___ mistake and lost all the data (CARE).
gaps.explanation: The suffix -less means without: careless means not taking care. It modifies the noun 'mistake'.

gaps.sentence: She gave a very ___ account of the incident that had everyone laughing (HUMOUR).
gaps.explanation: Everyone laughed, so the adjective is humorous (-ous). 'Humourless' means serious and would contradict the laughter.

gaps.sentence: The ___ of the new bridge will take two years (CONSTRUCT).
gaps.hint: noun needed as subject of the sentence
gaps.explanation: The subject needs a noun: construction (the -tion noun); 'constructive' is an adjective.

gaps.sentence: She is very ___ in modern art (INTEREST).
gaps.hint: how she feels: -ed; fixed pattern '___ in'
gaps.explanation: 'Interested in something' describes the person's feeling; 'interesting' describes the thing that causes it.

gaps.sentence: He ___ forgets to bring the tickets, as usual (TYPICAL).
gaps.hint: adverb of frequency needed to modify 'forgets' (-ly)
gaps.explanation: An adverb modifies the verb 'forgets': typically means in the usual way.

gaps.hint: noun needed after 'His'; note the -al suffix
gaps.explanation: The noun of 'refuse' is 'refusal' (-al noun); 'refuse' as a noun means rubbish.

gaps.sentence: We ___ the cost of the trip and ran out of money (ESTIMATE).
gaps.hint: judged it too low — that is why the money ran out (under-)
gaps.explanation: Running out of money shows the estimate was too low: underestimated (under- + estimated).
